caseStudies.title: Making pathology reports easier to understand
caseStudies.teaser: AI-powered analysis that turns complex pathology reports into clearer, structured insights.
caseStudies.challenge: Pathology reports arrived as dense, inconsistent narrative text, so reviewing one for the next clinical decision often took longer than the diagnosis itself.
challengePoints: Reports arrived as dense, inconsistent narrative text with no standard structure.
Reviewing one report for the next clinical decision often took longer than making the diagnosis itself.
Any fix had to slot into the clinicians' existing tools: no new software to learn.
caseStudies.approach: We built an AI layer that reads each report, extracts the clinically relevant findings, and restructures them into a consistent, scannable format the review team already recognized.

solutionPoints.title: Extraction pipeline
solutionPoints.body: An AI layer reads each incoming report and extracts the clinically relevant findings.

solutionPoints.title: Consistent structure
solutionPoints.body: Findings are restructured into a scannable format the review team already recognized.

solutionPoints.title: Fits existing tools
solutionPoints.body: Delivered inside the clinicians' current workflow, with no new software to learn.

caseStudies.result: Report review dropped from a first read to a confirmed summary 80% faster, with no change to the clinicians' existing tools.

benefits.title: 80% faster review
benefits.body: Report review dropped from a first read to a confirmed summary 80% faster.

benefits.title: No workflow disruption
benefits.body: Shipped with no change to the clinicians' existing tools.

benefits.title: Consistent output
benefits.body: Every report now follows the same scannable structure, regardless of how it arrived.

caseStudies.title: Turning sales calls into actionable coaching
caseStudies.teaser: An AI sales agent that scores rep performance, identifies what went wrong, and recommends ways to improve.
caseStudies.challenge: Managers could only sit in on a handful of calls a week, so most coaching happened days later, from memory, on the calls someone happened to catch.
challengePoints: Managers could only sit in on a handful of calls a week.
Most coaching happened days later, from memory, on whichever calls someone happened to catch.
Reps got feedback at the next weekly review, long after the call that needed it.
caseStudies.approach: We shipped an agent that listens to every call, scores it against the team's own playbook, and surfaces what went wrong with a timestamped clip, same day, not next review.

solutionPoints.title: Listens to every call
solutionPoints.body: An agent processes 100% of calls, not a manager-sampled handful.

solutionPoints.title: Scores against your playbook
solutionPoints.body: Each call is scored against the team's own playbook, not a generic rubric.

solutionPoints.title: Same-day, timestamped feedback
solutionPoints.body: Surfaces what went wrong with a timestamped clip, ready the same day.

caseStudies.result: 10K+ calls analyzed and counting, with coaching notes ready before the rep's next call instead of during a weekly review.

benefits.title: 10K+ calls analyzed
benefits.body: And counting: every call, not a sample.

benefits.title: Same-day coaching
benefits.body: Notes ready before the rep's next call, not during a weekly review.

benefits.title: Consistent scoring
benefits.body: Every call measured against the same playbook, not manager memory.

caseStudies.title: A conversational AI agent built to scale
caseStudies.teaser: Secure, production-ready AI deployed across web and mobile, with authentication, scaling, and observability built in.
caseStudies.challenge: Their support agent worked in a demo, but had none of the authentication, scaling or monitoring a security review, or a real launch, would require.
challengePoints: The support agent worked in a demo, but wasn't built for production.
No authentication, scaling, or monitoring: the basics a security review would require.
Needed to go live across both web and mobile without a rebuild from scratch.
caseStudies.approach: We rebuilt the agent on production infrastructure: proper auth, autoscaling under load, and full observability into every conversation it has.

solutionPoints.title: Production authentication
solutionPoints.body: Proper auth in front of every conversation, not a demo shortcut.

solutionPoints.title: Autoscaling under load
solutionPoints.body: Rebuilt to scale with real traffic instead of a fixed demo environment.

solutionPoints.title: Full observability
solutionPoints.body: Every conversation is monitored end to end, not just logged after the fact.

caseStudies.result: The agent now handles live customer conversations across web and mobile in production, with a security review already signed off.

benefits.title: Security review signed off
benefits.body: Passed the review a demo-grade agent couldn't have.

benefits.title: Live on web and mobile
benefits.body: Handles real customer conversations across both surfaces.

benefits.title: Production-grade from day one
benefits.body: Built to stay up under real load, not just demo traffic.

caseStudies.title: Scaling engineering simulations with cloud HPC
caseStudies.teaser: A high-performance AWS environment built for CPU-intensive CFD and GPU-accelerated DEM simulations.
caseStudies.challenge: Their simulation queue was bottlenecked on fixed on-prem hardware: CFD and DEM runs that should take hours were taking days waiting for a slot.
challengePoints: Simulation queue was bottlenecked on fixed on-prem hardware.
CFD and DEM runs that should take hours were taking days waiting for a slot.
Capacity was fixed to the rack, not to the actual workload.
caseStudies.approach: We designed a high-performance AWS environment purpose-built for CPU-intensive CFD and GPU-accelerated DEM workloads, elastic to the queue instead of a fixed rack.

solutionPoints.title: CPU-optimized CFD environment
solutionPoints.body: Purpose-built AWS environment for CPU-intensive CFD workloads.

solutionPoints.title: GPU-accelerated DEM
solutionPoints.body: Elastic GPU capacity for DEM simulations, provisioned on demand.

solutionPoints.title: Elastic to the queue
solutionPoints.body: Capacity scales to the workload instead of the workload waiting on a fixed rack.

caseStudies.result: Engineers now queue simulations on demand instead of waiting for hardware, with capacity that scales to the workload rather than the other way around.

benefits.title: Hours, not days
benefits.body: Simulations that waited days for a slot now run on demand.

benefits.title: Elastic capacity
benefits.body: Scales to the workload instead of the workload scaling to fixed hardware.

benefits.title: No more queue bottleneck
benefits.body: Engineers queue simulations on demand instead of waiting for hardware.

caseStudies.title: Cutting deploy time from hours to minutes
caseStudies.teaser: A legacy release process rebuilt around CI/CD and infrastructure as code, so shipping stopped depending on one engineer's calendar.
caseStudies.challenge: Every release meant one senior engineer manually running a checklist late at night, and a bad deploy could take hours to detect and roll back.
challengePoints: Deploys ran through a manual checklist only one engineer fully understood.
A bad release could take hours to detect and roll back.
Nobody wanted to ship on a Friday, so releases piled up.
caseStudies.approach: We replaced the manual checklist with a CI/CD pipeline and infrastructure as code, plus automated rollback triggered by the same health checks the team already trusted.

solutionPoints.title: CI/CD pipeline
solutionPoints.body: Every merge to main runs the same automated build, test, and deploy sequence, no manual checklist.

solutionPoints.title: Infrastructure as code
solutionPoints.body: Environments are reproducible from a repo, not a runbook in someone's head.

solutionPoints.title: Automated rollback
solutionPoints.body: A failed health check reverts the release automatically, before an engineer has to notice.

caseStudies.result: Deploys dropped from a multi-hour, one-person process to a 12-minute pipeline anyone on the team can trigger.

benefits.title: 12-minute deploys
benefits.body: Down from a multi-hour manual process.

benefits.title: No more single point of failure
benefits.body: Any engineer on the team can ship a release.

benefits.title: Automatic rollback
benefits.body: Bad releases revert themselves before they reach most users.

caseStudies.title: An agent that replans routes when a delivery falls through
caseStudies.teaser: A multi-agent system that reassigns and replans delivery routes in real time, instead of a dispatcher doing it by hand.
caseStudies.challenge: When a driver called in or a delivery window slipped, a dispatcher had to manually re-sequence a dozen other routes by hand, under time pressure.
challengePoints: One disruption meant manually re-sequencing a dozen other routes.
Dispatchers made the call under time pressure, with incomplete visibility.
The same disruption pattern repeated daily, with no system learning from it.
caseStudies.approach: We built a multi-agent system that monitors live delivery status, detects a disruption, and re-plans affected routes automatically, with a dispatcher approving before anything changes.

solutionPoints.title: Live disruption detection
solutionPoints.body: Agents watch delivery status in real time and flag a disruption the moment it happens.

solutionPoints.title: Automatic re-planning
solutionPoints.body: Affected routes are re-sequenced by the agent, not rebuilt by hand under pressure.

solutionPoints.title: Human approval checkpoint
solutionPoints.body: A dispatcher signs off before a changed route goes live.

caseStudies.result: Disruptions that used to cost 20+ minutes of manual re-planning now resolve in under two minutes, with a dispatcher only approving, not building, the fix.

benefits.title: 20+ min saved per disruption
benefits.body: Re-planning that took a dispatcher 20+ minutes now takes under two.

benefits.title: Fewer missed windows
benefits.body: Faster replanning means fewer delivery windows blown by a single disruption.

benefits.title: Dispatcher stays in control
benefits.body: Every change is approved by a human before it ships.

caseStudies.title: Making a contract library searchable in plain English
caseStudies.teaser: A retrieval pipeline that lets associates ask a contract library a question and get a cited answer, instead of searching by keyword.
caseStudies.challenge: Associates searched thousands of contracts by keyword and still had to open a dozen documents to confirm one clause was standard.
challengePoints: Keyword search returned dozens of documents for one question.
Confirming a clause was standard meant opening and comparing several contracts by hand.
Nothing traced an answer back to the exact clause it came from.
caseStudies.approach: We indexed the firm's contract library into a retrieval pipeline that answers a plain-English question with the relevant clauses and a citation back to the source document.

solutionPoints.title: Retrieval pipeline
solutionPoints.body: The full contract library indexed and retrievable by meaning, not just keyword.

solutionPoints.title: Grounded, cited answers
solutionPoints.body: Every answer points back to the exact clause and document it came from.

solutionPoints.title: Evaluation dashboard
solutionPoints.body: Ongoing measurement against a set of questions the practice group actually asks.

caseStudies.result: A question that took an associate 20-30 minutes of manual search now gets a cited answer in under a minute.

benefits.title: Minutes, not half an hour
benefits.body: Clause lookups that took 20-30 minutes now resolve in under a minute.

benefits.title: Every answer cited
benefits.body: Associates can verify the source clause instead of trusting a summary.

benefits.title: Scales with the library
benefits.body: Adding new contracts doesn't add new manual search time.

caseStudies.title: Proving an underwriting model before funding the build
caseStudies.teaser: A scoped proof of concept on real loan data, answering whether an AI underwriting assist could work before the board funded a production build.
caseStudies.challenge: The team believed an AI-assisted underwriting model could speed up approvals, but couldn't get budget without proof it worked on their actual, messy loan data.
challengePoints: Leadership wouldn't fund a build without evidence it worked on real data.
Prior AI demos elsewhere in the business had been thrown away after the pilot.
The team had weeks, not quarters, to make the case.
caseStudies.approach: We built a scoped proof of concept directly against the lender's historical loan data, then gave a direct read-out on accuracy, edge cases, and what production would take.

solutionPoints.title: Scoped POC on real data
solutionPoints.body: Built and tested against the lender's actual historical loan applications.

solutionPoints.title: Feasibility read-out
solutionPoints.body: A direct answer on where the model performed and where it didn't.

solutionPoints.title: Path to production
solutionPoints.body: Architected so a green light meant extending the POC, not rebuilding it.

caseStudies.result: The board approved production funding off a working proof of concept in three weeks, and the POC's architecture became the first production build.

benefits.title: Funded off a working proof
benefits.body: Board sign-off came from a real result, not a slide deck.

benefits.title: No thrown-away work
benefits.body: The POC's code became the start of the production system.

benefits.title: Clear-eyed on limits
benefits.body: The read-out was honest about where the model needed guardrails.

caseStudies.title: A copilot that drafts the answer before support has to
caseStudies.teaser: An in-product copilot that drafts a reply to the same five questions support was answering all day, tuned to the product's own tone.
caseStudies.challenge: Support tickets were overwhelmingly the same five questions, but every reply was still typed out by hand in a tone that varied by agent.
challengePoints: The same five questions made up most of the support queue.
Every reply was still typed by hand, in a tone that varied by agent.
Users asked mid-workflow, not in a separate help tab.
caseStudies.approach: We embedded a copilot directly in the product that drafts a reply in the team's tone, pulling from the same answers support already gives, with an agent reviewing before it sends.

solutionPoints.title: Conversation design
solutionPoints.body: Scripted around the actual five questions, not a generic FAQ bot.

solutionPoints.title: In-product integration
solutionPoints.body: Lives inside the app where the user already is, not a separate widget.

solutionPoints.title: Usage analytics
solutionPoints.body: Visibility into which drafts agents edit, so the copilot keeps improving.

caseStudies.result: First-response time on the top five ticket types dropped by more than half, with agents editing instead of writing from scratch.

benefits.title: 50%+ faster first response
benefits.body: On the ticket types that made up most of the queue.

benefits.title: Consistent tone
benefits.body: Every drafted reply matches the same voice, regardless of which agent sends it.

benefits.title: Agents review, not write
benefits.body: Agents edit a drafted answer instead of typing one from scratch.
